In light of the above, both sides have extensively argued on the arbitrability of the dispute involved in the present case and whether this Commission has jurisdiction to deal with the dispute involved or is mandatorily required to refer it to arbitration. Based on the submissions of the parties, the issues that arise for our decision are discussed in the subsequent paragraphs. 15. The Petitioner has primarily contended that the reliefs claimed in the matter pertain to termination of the PPA and thus qualify as a non-tariff dispute in terms of the DVC Judgment, wherein it has _i) Where any Dispute (a) arises from a claim made by any Party for any change in or determination of the Tariff or any matter related to Tariff or claims made by any Party which partly or wholly relate to any change in the Tariff or determination of any of such claims could result in change in the Tariff, or (b) relates to any matter agreed to be referred to the Appropriate Commission, such Dispute shall be submitted to adjudication by the Appropriate Commission._ _ The jurisdictional facts, necessary for the CERC to exercise its powers of adjudication of the dispute under Section 79(1)(f) read with Section 79(1)(a), is firstly that the dispute involves a generating company owned or controlled by the Central Government; secondly that the dispute is in regard to matters connected with the power of the CERC to regulate _ **_4 SCC 539, etc_** . The Respondents have also argued that the Petitioner has not filed any formal application for reference of the dispute to arbitration and has sought such reference only through a written note dated 10.01.2025. of the Act, the Commission is required to refer to such disputes to the arbitration. The relevant - (i) The primary/principal dispute involved the Petitioner and Respondents in the present Petition does not relate to tariff or regulation of tariff and such dispute, thus, does not fall within the ambit of adjudicatory jurisdiction of this Commission under Section 79(1)(f) read with Section 79(1)(b) of the Act. Keeping in view the nature of the dispute and the value involved in the Petition, the Commission finds it appropriate to refer the dispute(s) between the contracting parties to a panel comprising three arbitrators as per Regulation 49(b) of the COB Regulations, 2023. Accordingly, both the contracting parties shall suggest the names of the arbitrators in terms of the said Regulation within two weeks from the date of this order, and the third arbitrator shall be nominated based on the suggestions of both the nominated arbitrators.
